primitives.name: Iterative RDP Segmentation
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Segment ID assignment:** iterative RDP: Υ_i = RDP(X_i, ε); marks significant points (beginning/end, then recursively the point with max perpendicular distance d(x_{i,k},x_{i,s},x_{i,e}) exceeding ε); each timestep gets a segment ID υ_{i,t}.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'Υ_i': 'Set of significant points for trajectory i', 'ε': 'Distance threshold (dimensionless)', 'x_{i,k}': 'K-th point in trajectory i', 'x_{i,s}': 'Start point of segment', 'x_{i,e}': 'End point of segment', 'υ_{i,t}': 'Segment ID for timestep t in trajectory i'}
primitives.assumptions: RDP identifies operationally meaningful waypoints; segments reflect shared contextual behavior.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When ε approaches zero, all points become significant; when ε exceeds path variation, only start/end remain.

layer2.mapping: Each segment ID corresponds to a movement primitive (cut, break, stem) in GSE's motion graph.
layer2.telemetry: Segment boundary alignment with charted flight instructions.

primitives.name: Causal Transformer Encoder
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Causal Transformer encoder** (GPT-2/3 style, NoPos — no explicit positional encoding, L2 norm after projections): 12 layers, d=768, FFN 3072 (GELU), 12 heads, dropout 0.35; binomial timestamp masking p=0.2 applied BEFORE input projection (mimics missing states from irregular transmissions); representation dim 320.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'Z': 'Encoded trajectory representation (dim 320)', 'X_{\\text{masked}}': 'Input trajectory with masked timestamps', 'p': 'Masking probability (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Trajectory states are causally ordered; masking simulates real-world irregularity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Incomplete trajectories cause embedding drift; masking ensures robustness.

layer2.mapping: Encodes temporal dependencies into fixed-dimensional embeddings for downstream clustering and classification tasks.
layer2.telemetry: Embedding drift under partial trajectory input.

primitives.name: Soft Nearest Neighbor Loss
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Soft Nearest Neighbor loss:** batch flattened to Z_f (ΣT_i vectors); segment IDs remapped per batch; L_snn = -E[log Σ_{j:υ_i=υ_j} exp(z_iTz_j/τ) - log Σ_{k:υ_i≠υ_k} exp(z_iTz_k/τ)] — positives = same segment (within/across instances), negatives = different segments; positives excluded from the negative sum (modified form).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'L_{\\text{snn}}': 'Soft nearest neighbor loss (scalar)', 'z_i, z_j': 'Trajectory embeddings', 'τ': 'Temperature parameter (dimensionless)', 'υ_i': 'Segment ID of trajectory i'}
primitives.assumptions: Positive pairs are defined by shared segment identity; negatives exclude same-segment matches.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Loss diverges when τ→0 or embeddings collapse into singleton clusters.

layer2.mapping: Maps trajectory embeddings to semantic clusters aligned with flight concept categories.
layer2.telemetry: Clustering NMI/ARI against charted runway/corridor classes.

The ATSCC framework defines trajectory similarity through geometric segmentation using iterative RDP, which partitions trajectories into operationally meaningful segments. This approach avoids reliance on data augmentation, which is unreliable for temporal dynamics. The causal transformer encodes these segments into fixed-dimensional representations, enabling real-time processing without explicit positional encoding. The Soft Nearest Neighbor loss enforces that embeddings of points within the same segment are pulled together while pushing apart those from different segments. These primitives form a coherent system where geometric structure induces semantic meaning, allowing for unsupervised clustering of flight paths into concepts such as routes, corridors, and maneuvers. The framework's strength lies in its ability to generalize across datasets due to its reliance on geometric inductive bias rather than domain-specific augmentations. Failure modes include misalignment between RDP breakpoints and actual waypoints, or insufficient training data leading to poor generalization of segment embeddings.
